items.note: Story 1: Association organized by Gideon Vose at Larrow Green 1889; main creamery 1891.
Story 1: Article VII paid on butterfat by test, not weight; test at point of delivery governs.
Story 2: because payment was by test, the low test was a running loss of real money.
Teague as bookkeeper (Story 6) and Sill as Larrow Green buttermaker (Story 7) are named. Effie Loomis is absent. List item with no REQUIRED line, so credited on its core fact.
Section A calls Selby Vose only 'the new manager' in 1919. It never calls him Gideon's son and never gives 1913. The son relationship appears only in B3.
Section A mentions station-gain entries and a heavy-cream ledger pattern but gives neither the 1898 origin nor the ~5.25% shape.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Section A never describes the weigh / composite-sample / fixed-charge / graduated-neck mechanism.
Story 1: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 1: six dozen pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93. The 17.6 c.c. mark is in Story 8.
Story 8: a short pipette gives the same proportional short charge every time, so the fault was constant year-round.
The point that the pipette cannot be checked without a burette, and none was in the county, is absent.
Keddie 1861-1934, tester twenty-nine seasons from the opening, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Story 4: station test book, all patrons, kept by Ansel Keddie in his own hand.
The summary leaf's 1896 = 3.80 is never given. Story 4 even calls 3.61 the 'true average'.
Story 3: broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. No 3.80 figure, but this is a list item with no REQUIRED line, credited on its core fact.
Story 5: married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Story 5: died 1934 still under suspicion.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Brant the largest.
Story 4 gives '1 Jan 1897 or 1 Jan 1898', calls it unresolved, and leans toward r09's 1898. It does not settle on 1 January 1897. The scales agreeing is present.
Story 2 resolves the visible Hollow-vs-valley complaint gap as 0.19, which is the conflation that loses this item by rule.
Story 2: Grigg committee, January-March 1908, wet-hay explanation reported as the committee's finding.
It has 200,000 lb at 3.42, but Story 4 treats the loss as a flat additive 0.19 (380 lb) rather than proportional. 'Proportional' is bolded and contradicted.
Story 4: passed to Roy, lent (not given) to Ivy in 1958, Hazel later.
Story 7: Alder Corners Cheese Company, over the ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd. Redlow is not named, but the item has no REQUIRED line.
Story 7: four of six farms hauled there in the summer flush, 1915-1930.
Independence elements: other county (Vessey), own glassware, never compared figures.
It gives Alder Corners averages of 3.78-3.82 over sixteen seasons but never states that the same milk tested about 0.19 higher than at Ostrey Hollow.
Story 7: the same patrons' milk tested elsewhere was never thin or watered, which disposes of both explanations.
Rosalie Cudd, daughter, ran the factory after 1941, supplied Ivy with the 1915-1930 run in 1958.
Strawn is never named in Section A, only 'the state dairy inspector'. No circuit span given.
The lactometer point appears only in Section F. Nothing in Section A.
Story 8: inspector condemned the glassware, best-dated 12 June 1923. Burette-in-1923 not stated; credited on the core fact.
Absent.
Section A has no replacement-order dates and no 1924 average of 3.80. The rise is mentioned only in F and C.
The crate in the loft is present, but the notebooks going to the college library in 1947 are absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Story 6: petitioned January 1925.
Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Watering (manager), cream theft (Teague), wet hay (1908 report). Board found no cause.
The four exhibits are listed, but Section A never says the 1923 notebook contained the answer and was read for other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; $3,800 'without admission' four days later. The account charged is A7.6's aspect.
No one-fifth-of-$19,000 point and no charge to the station-gain account in Section A.
Ivy Keddie b. 1931, granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, under Leland Vaught.
Section A never says she assembled records that had never been in the same room. That idea appears only in G.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, one part in twenty. The 0.88 is not stated in A, but the item has no REQUIRED line.
Story 8: proportional one-in-twenty shortfall, 3.61 recorded vs 3.80 true, from 1 May 1897 to replacement in 1923.
None of 40M lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 or the ledger identity appears in Section A.

Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, cleared him twenty-four years after his death. The 35- and 33-year intervals are absent, but the item has no REQUIRED line. Story 5's '1948, twenty-four years before' is an internal slip.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy's father (r18).
Second cousins via Duncan and Roy as first cousins.
Full vs half sibling declared unresolved and does not change the answer. Leans toward r09 while explicitly declining.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote Article VII, which made every test a money matter; his son looked for the fault in the patrons, not the equipment.
Asserts 'None... I resolve for no relationship' (A01 asserted).
An asserted abstention item scores 0. It also never states that no document names or denies the link.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, one part in twenty.
$95.00 (380 x $0.25). Key $86.40; $90 accepted only from 360 lb at 25 cents.
States ~1,520,000 lb (by extrapolation), matching the key's figure.
Gives 5.25% of the credited amount (the true value is 5.26%). Neither 76,000 as the difference nor 5.00% of delivered fat is given.
$77.93 with itemized sum.
72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c.
Says 'roughly 26 years' instead of the exact 26 years 6 weeks. The reason given for 25 vs 26 is wrong: it blames the excluded 1896 season rather than the 1897 and 1923 part years.
Cannot be determined; the two memories conflict and no ledger figure exists.
Variable: the measuring instrument, own broken glass replaced by a borrowed measure.
Herds, patrons, pasture/season, tester, supervision.
Says only 'rose markedly... fell back'. Never gives 3.80 through the interval or 3.61 after.
Establishes the fault travels with the instrument, not milk, cows, patrons or tester. Limit: not the size or mechanism.
1911 interval (tester's own book), ledger surplus (r02/r05/r23), Alder Corners (r10) and Sill (r14).
Shows independence by record-keeping system and says all three hold without the 1958 measurement.
Asserts 'No' on whether Teague questioned the entries (A09 asserted).
Yes, he knew the station tested low: grievance and 1919 circular.
Signed the station-gain ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the 1925 hearing (Story 6/F). Its 'from 1911' is wrong but three elements are met.

'Sources give no evidence he knew its cause' is not a declared inability to settle. It relies on Kyle's single account without the two opposed office narrators or the other required observations. Not an assertion, so no deduction.
1908 sampling (row 2: report vs covering letter); Rosalie daughter vs niece (own letter); arbitration 1925 vs 1924; also second cousins vs once removed.
Pairs named with breakers: 3.16 (r05, r13; arithmetic), eleven pipettes (r12, r19), five dozen (r11, r21), 12 July (r08, r12), 1898 (r11, r23), 44M (r05, r12), $3,500 (r01, r21).
A04 leans to accident ('most plausibly... mold reground') without abstaining. A06 is not addressed. A10 is abstained only in Section A (Story 1), not in B-G.
r11's 16.27 cascade vs its own quoted 'one part in twenty' conclusion; also r15's 'whole of 1908' vs its reprinted report.
Names the pipettes and proportional error, but treats 0.19 as a constant additive (C2b, Story 4) rather than 5% of 3.80. Does not give the 1896-on-borrowed-glass onset evidence.
Watering (Vose) defeated by the lactometer and Alder Corners.
Theft (Teague) defeated by cream arriving heavier every year in his own ledger.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, against a constant 0.19.
Answers 'No.' on whether the board examined the glass (A07 asserted).
Asserts that Keddie privately suspected the patrons, on r13 (A05 asserted; also in Story 5).
Summary is about 168 words, over the 150-word limit.
Only four series named: ledgers, weigh book, inspector's notebook, 1958 bulletin/measurement. 'Diaries' and 'oral histories' are not keyed series.
No decoy stated as fact and no wrong headline number.
Has 1897, $19,000 and 1958, only three of six. It never gives 1923 and names neither Ansel nor Ivy.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Strawn's circuit visits 'from 1908 forward' asserted (F)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as 'no relationship' (B4, E17)
Gullibility A09: Teague never questioned the entries asserted (D2)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware asserted 'No.' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester privately believed the patrons at fault asserted (F, Story 5)
